# Two Different Mechanisms in the Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV, the EPA’s Acid Rain Program addressed sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector through distinct mechanisms and timelines.

For sulfur dioxide, the program used an aggregate cap and tradable allowances. Each allowance covered one ton of sulfur dioxide, while the cap set the permitted total—it was not a measure of reported actual emissions. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap in 2010 was 8.95 million tons.

The nitrogen oxides component followed a different approach. It began in 1996 and applied a rate-based rule to certain coal-fired units; it did not introduce a cap or allowance trading. The two pollutants were therefore governed by different mechanisms on different timelines.
